subject: Performance annex and evidence playbook request for Veridian deployment
messages:
From: Angela Ruiz <angela.ruiz@veridianhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Performance annex and evidence requirements for Veridian deployment

Hi Monica,

Thanks for taking this up. As we work toward finalizing the MSA and order form for the upcoming Veridian production rollout, Legal/Procurement has asked for a concrete performance annex that ties uptime/latency commitments to remedies and the evidence path for any credits. High level asks from our side: 

- Explicit uptime SLA and credit schedule for monthly availability (we're proposing a two-tier credit schedule if missed).
- P99 latency SLO for API endpoints used by our CareOps workflows and how Redwood measures it (ingress e2e vs token-level).
- Accepted evidence types to substantiate outage/latency breaches (traces, per-customer token logs, infra events, internal health checks).
- Retention windows for audit logs and whether Redwood will provide a downloadable evidence package on request.
- A short mutual-action plan for escalation and programmatic fallback (model variant routing).

Can you point us to a draft of the performance annex you usually attach to the order form and confirm the order form clause IDs we should expect in the procurement packet? We need to circulate to Legal and Infrastructure by Friday so they can vet the remedies language and evidence path.

Appreciate a quick call if that helps — Angela Ruiz, Veridian Procurement (contracts@veridianhealth.com).

Thanks,
Angela

--
Angela Ruiz
Director, Procurement
Veridian Health
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Angela Ruiz <angela.ruiz@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-16T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance annex and evidence requirements for Veridian deployment

Hi Angela —

Thanks for the clear list. I can absolutely share our standard performance annex and a procurement playbook that enumerates acceptable evidence types and the delivery process for evidence packages. Quick answers up front:

- Uptime: our standard is 99.95% monthly for Hosted API; we can discuss a 99.9% commitment for this account with a defined credit schedule in the annex and order form.
- Latency: we publish P95/P99 tail latency measurements measured at the API ingress (end-to-end request latency) — we can provide both token-level timing and end-to-end traces on request.
- Evidence: we accept traces, request-level logs (redacted to remove PHI), per-tenant token counts, and cluster health events. We produce a compressed evidence bundle for procurement review.
- Retention: standard retention for audit logs is 180 days; extended retention can be added in Private deployments or via an add-on.

I'm attaching a working draft (proposed-performance-annex_v3.docx) and the Redwood_OrderForm_Draft.pdf with placeholder clause IDs. Please review and flag any specific redlines. If Legal wants to see a sample evidence bundle, I can forward a sanitized Veridian-like bundle (filename Veridian_Verified_RTO_RPO_evidence.zip) under an NDA.

If that sounds good, can we book a 30-minute call tomorrow at 10am PT to walk through the annex and any evidence expectations?

Best,
Monica

--

Date: 2028-05-16T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Legal redlines: uptime credit schedule (RE: Performance annex)

Monica —

Forwarding a quick note from our Legal team with some initial redline points. High level: they want the credit schedule to include a graduated credit (5%/10% of monthly fees) and an explicit carve-out for customer-caused latency (burden of proof tied to our own synthetic tests). Also asking for a clearer evidence timeline — "we need evidence within 5 business days of the claim."

Fwd below: 

On Thu, May 16, 2028 at 12:58 PM Legal <legal@veridianhealth.com> wrote:
> Team,
>

> - Defines monthly availability buckets with corresponding credits;
> - Requires Redwood to provide a detailed evidence bundle within 5 business days after a written credit request;
> - Adds a customer-contributed-fault clause (burden of proof split) so we can avoid credits when upstream customer actions are the proximate cause.
>
> --Veridian Legal
>
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Matt O'Connell <matt.oconnell@veridianhealth.com>, Angela Ruiz <angela.ruiz@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance annex and evidence requirements for Veridian deployment

Hi Matt/Angela —

Thanks for the detail. Legal side at Redwood (cc'd) here — a couple of clarifications and a suggested path: 

1) Evidence timeline and scope: Redwood can commit to assembling and delivering a compressed evidence bundle within 5 business days of a validated credit request. The bundle will include: 
   - API request logs (per-tenant) with timestamps and unique request IDs (redacted for PHI)
   - Ingress+egress traces showing end-to-end latency spans
   - Cluster health and autoscale events from the affected region
   - Our internal incident timeline and mitigation notes

2) Customer-contributed-fault: we are open to an explicit clause that allows us to deny credits when the root cause is customer configuration or third-party integrations. Proposed language will require a joint RCA within 10 business days; if the joint RCA concludes Redwood is not at fault, no credit is issued.

3) Measurement baseline: we'll provide both Redwood's ingress measurements and an agreed synthetic test harness (we can supply a simple script and location for you to run to capture e2e baseline). For the Veridian rollout, I suggest P99 latency measured at ingress for production traffic and synthetic P99 where applicable.

4) Retention and export: standard 180-day retention for logs. For this engagement we can include a one-time 12-month retention export for evidence purposes as part of the order form add-on.

I'll attach a proposed evidence checklist and a redline of the annex language after our internal redline pass later today. Monica — happy to join the call and walk Legal/Infra through the checklist.

Regards,
Naomi

--
Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
